findings.title: Wire the new timeout setting into the shutdown drain
findings.problem: A supported value such as shutdown_drain_timeout=120.5 is accepted but ignored. search/scheduler.py:70–81 derives _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT solely from the environment or a hardcoded 60.0, and line 634 uses that constant. With no environment override, shutdown therefore stops waiting after 60 seconds and closes clients and the database even when the operator configured a longer drain for an active search.
findings.why_it_matters: A supported value such as shutdown_drain_timeout=120.5 is accepted but ignored. search/scheduler.py:70–81 derives _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT solely from the environment or a hardcoded 60.0, and line 634 uses that constant. With no environment override, shutdown therefore stops waiting after 60 seconds and closes clients and the database even when the operator configured a longer drain for an active search.
findings.fix_hint: Use settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout as the shutdown default, retaining the environment override, and add a lifecycle test proving a nondefault configuration reaches the drain timeout.
source_window: # Defense in depth: a TOML inf cannot unbound the drain. Config value is the default;
# TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT env overrides at shutdown; form clamp (3600.0) is the UI ceiling.
shutdown_drain_timeout: float = Field(default=60.0, ge=1.0, allow_inf_nan=False)
# v2.2: skip Radarr movies without past digital/physical release date
skip_unreleased: bool = True

members.title: shutdown_drain_timeout config field is validated but never read by the shutdown drain
members.problem: Nothing reads the new field. The only use of the drain timeout is the module constant `_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT = _read_shutdown_drain_timeout()` at triggarr/search/scheduler.py:81. It is computed at import time from the env var alone and used at scheduler.py:611-656. A grep for `shutdown_drain_timeout` finds no consumer outside the model and tests/test_config.py. The comment on the changed line says 'Config value is the default; TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT env overrides at shutdown', but that precedence is not implemented, so a user-set TOML value is silently ignored. pending: confirm this is not just an unfinished step of phase 75 (HEAD is the 'add failing test' commit, so the scheduler wiring may land in a later plan).

members.fix_hint: change _read_shutdown_drain_timeout to take settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout as the default, apply the env override on top, and call it at shutdown time instead of at import
members.intent_doc_match: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-02-recovery-counts-config-design.md:173-175 says the scheduler must read settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout and then apply the env override on top

members.title: The config field has no upper bound, and the 3600.0 'form clamp' named in the comment does not exist yet
members.problem: The field only sets ge=1.0, with no le= limit. A TOML edit such as 1e9 passes validation. The comment says 'form clamp (3600.0) is the UI ceiling', but grep finds no such clamp in triggarr/web yet. Hand-edited TOML would not go through it anyway. In practice, Docker's stop_grace_period (90s in the README and docker-compose.yml) SIGKILLs the process before any large drain value matters, so the effect is limited. pending: confirm whether a model-level le= limit is wanted or the form clamp alone is intended.

members.why_it_matters: If the drain timeout exceeds the container stop grace period, the process gets SIGKILLed partway through the drain. The bound mainly makes that limit explicit.

members.title: No upper bound on shutdown_drain_timeout at the model layer; values above stop_grace_period are cut off by SIGKILL
members.problem: The field has ge=1.0 but no le. The comment says only the form clamps to 3600.0, so a hand-edited TOML file (or a config loaded outside the form) can set any finite value, for example 600. docker-compose.yml:24 and the README document stop_grace_period: 90s, which must exceed the drain timeout. Any configured value above about 90 means Docker sends SIGKILL in the middle of the drain. pending: confirm this is intended, and whether the UI/docs should warn that values above the container grace period are ineffective.
